newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 23.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh women hold eight percent of ministerial positions against the global percentage of seven and regional four, says a UNICEF report.
Rohingya refugees on Tuesday demonstrated in a camp expressing their unwillingness to return to Burma.
Ruling Awami League has called upon its leaders and workers to resist fundamentalist forces in the country.
A general trade sgreement between Bangladesh and South Africa is expected to be signed shortly.

The government has decided to take legal action against the chief clergy of Baitul Mukarram national mosque for his involvement in a incident in which some people threw slippers on the dias where President Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed was sitting.
Fifty percent of Bangladeshi babies are born underweight compared to 20 percent in developing countries.
The construction of the proposed Ganges barrage will get priority in the fifth five year plan (1997-2002).
A 19-member trade delegation, led by Commerce and Industries Minister Toafel Ahmed, left Dhaka for Bangkok on Tuesday on a four-day visit to Thailand. REUTER
